verses.author: model_A
verses.text: She folds the letter twice before deciding not to send it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles anyway
on the desk she meant to clear —
some things arrive by staying.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle forgets it boiled,
cools quiet on the stove —
some things arrive by leaving.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A moth taps the window twice
then finds another dark to fold itself into —
not all doors are meant to open.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Snow gathers on the sill unread,
melts before the morning claims it —
some things arrive by vanishing.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A phone lights up at midnight,
no message, just the glow —
some things arrive by almost.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light hums to no one,
moths already gone —
some things stay by forgetting why.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle forgets it boiled,
steam gone before the tea is poured —
warmth doesn't wait to be noticed.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A door left off the latch all night,
no wind, no thief, just habit —
some things stay open out of hope.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The mirror keeps last summer's light
long after the room goes dark —
some things shine on borrowed time.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The calendar still marks a birthday
of someone who moved away —
some things count on out of loyalty.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dog waits by the door at five,
though no one's coming home that way now —
some things keep faith without asking why.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle's set for two each morning,
one cup left standing, going cold —
some things still hope to be needed.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The porch light stays on past midnight,
though the traveler took the other road —
some things keep watch out of habit alone.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The old dog's leash still hangs by the door,
looped just so, ready for a hand —
some things wait longer than they should.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I stop making four when I bake bread,
break one loaf smaller now to fit —
some things learn to want less, slowly.
